## boundary-reviewer:subprocess-interpolation:ddb9cac3

```yaml
blocker_id: boundary-reviewer:subprocess-interpolation:ddb9cac3
section_anchor: behaviors-13
finding_class: defect
reviewer_count: 1
```

**Reviewer:** boundary-reviewer

```
The spec says only that gh is "invoked with an argv array". It does not say how issue titles, bodies, comments and field values reach `gh api graphql`. These are filer-controlled or board-supplied strings. If they go through `-F`/`--field`, gh treats a value starting with `@` as a local file to read, so a title or note like `@/path/to/secret` would upload that file to GitHub. If the GraphQL document is built by interpolating them, that is the string-built-command risk behind `assertSafeArgvToken`, which cannot be applied to free text. Recommendation: require a constant GraphQL document with every value passed as a variable, via raw `-f` or `--input -` with a JSON body on stdin, never `-F`. Add a test that a value beginning with `@` or containing shell metacharacters is transmitted literally. State that the transport accepts no caller-supplied argv tokens beyond the fixed `gh api graphql` shape.
```

BEH-37 runs the same contract cases against json and github, and reopen is not among the documented github-only differences. Question: should the github adapter keep the shared closed-issue rules, or reopen as a documented github-only difference? Options: (a) conform: update() on a closed item throws ISSUE_CLOSED and status closed throws USE_CLOSE_METHOD, dropping reopen; (b) keep reopen, add it to BEH-37's github-only cases, and amend issue-epic-crud.spec.md.
